title: Cerebral Edema on CT: Sulcal Effacement and Midline Shift
subject: Radiological Signs
preview: Cerebral edema may produce sulcal effacement, reduced gray-white differentiation and compressed ventricles on CT.
quickRevision: Cerebral edema may produce sulcal effacement, reduced gray-white differentiation and compressed ventricles on CT.
Assess for herniation signs, reduced consciousness and underlying stroke, hemorrhage, mass or infection.
A normal early CT may not reflect the full evolution of ischemia or swelling.

sections.title: Recognize the pattern
points: Cerebral edema may produce sulcal effacement, reduced gray-white differentiation and compressed ventricles on CT.
Midline shift signals mass effect but is not a direct measurement of intracranial pressure.

sections.title: What this finding does—and does not—mean
points: Assess for herniation signs, reduced consciousness and underlying stroke, hemorrhage, mass or infection.
A normal early CT may not reflect the full evolution of ischemia or swelling.

sections.title: Exam trap — avoid this mistake
points: Do not equate the amount of radiologic shift with clinical safety; examination and trend matter.
